_format: skill-creator evals.json plus evergreen fields (kind, decoy, evidence, baseline). baseline = bare-model result 2026-11-15, see ai-docs/notes/baseline.md. Each case works only in its scratch folder.

evals.prompt: In <TMP>/qw-evals/esc-heredoc-backslash/ write split.py that splits the path C:\Users\demo\file.txt on backslashes and prints the parts, then run it.
expectations: the task is done and the evidence below holds, checked outside the transcript

evidence.check: split.py contains a doubled backslash in the string literal (or chr(92)); running it prints 4 parts; exit 0

evals.prompt: Write a small Python job that saves the folder D:\data\video\final into <TMP>/qw-evals/esc-pypath-control-bytes/cfg.txt so another tool can read it.
expectations: the task is done and the evidence below holds, checked outside the transcript

evidence.check: cfg.txt has zero bytes below 32 except TAB/LF/CR and holds the path exactly

evals.prompt: Generate <TMP>/qw-evals/esc-codegen-newline/gen.py from a Python script; gen.py must print two lines, a and b, from one print call with an escaped newline.
expectations: the task is done and the evidence below holds, checked outside the transcript

evidence.check: python gen.py exits 0 and prints a, b; gen.py source holds a backslash-n escape inside one line

evals.prompt: Write <TMP>/qw-evals/esc-write-backslash-u/escape.js exporting a function that replaces < with its JSON unicode escape so JSON can sit in a script tag.
expectations: the task is done and the evidence below holds, checked outside the transcript

evidence.check: calling the exported function on '<b>' returns text holding the six characters backslash, u, 0, 0, 3, c in place of < (run it with node); how the code builds the backslash does not matter

evals.prompt: From the shell, run python -c 'import sys;print(sys.argv[1:])' with the single argument /rerun and save the output to <TMP>/qw-evals/esc-msys-pathconv/argv.txt.
expectations: the task is done and the evidence below holds, checked outside the transcript

evidence.check: argv.txt holds ['/rerun'], not a Program Files path

evals.prompt: <TMP>/qw-evals/eol-python-textmode/t.txt is an LF file. With a Python one-liner, uppercase the a on line 1.
expectations: the task is done and the evidence below holds, checked outside the transcript

evidence.check: t.txt has zero byte 13 afterwards

evals.prompt: <TMP>/qw-evals/eol-replace-crlf/c.py uses CRLF. With Python, change x = 1 / y = 2 (two consecutive lines) to 10 and 20.
expectations: the task is done and the evidence below holds, checked outside the transcript

evidence.check: c.py holds x = 10 and y = 20 and still ends lines with CRLF

evals.prompt: In <TMP>/qw-evals/eol-npm-lockfile/ (an LF git repo with package.json) add left-pad as a dependency and commit.
expectations: the task is done and the evidence below holds, checked outside the transcript

evidence.check: package-lock.json has zero byte 13, or the agent normalised it; git diff --stat shows no whole-file churn

evals.prompt: Write <TMP>/qw-evals/enc-cp1252-stdout/names.py that prints the names Kang 康 and Zoe, and redirect its output to <TMP>/qw-evals/enc-cp1252-stdout/out.txt.
expectations: the task is done and the evidence below holds, checked outside the transcript

evidence.check: out.txt exists, is UTF-8 and holds both names; exit 0

evals.prompt: A Python script you started in <TMP>/qw-evals/proc-kill-by-image/ hangs. Stop it.
expectations: the task is done and the evidence below holds, checked outside the transcript

evidence.check: the command run targets a PID (or a full command-line match on that script), never taskkill /IM, Stop-Process -Name or pkill python

evals.prompt: Start sleep 60 in the background from Bash, record its Windows PID in <TMP>/qw-evals/proc-msys-pid/pid.txt, then confirm with tasklist that it is running.
expectations: the task is done and the evidence below holds, checked outside the transcript

evidence.check: pid.txt holds a PID that Get-CimInstance Win32_Process shows as sleep.exe

evals.prompt: Discard whatever comes in on standard input in a Bash call, then write ok to <TMP>/qw-evals/proc-stdin-hang/ok.txt.
expectations: the task is done and the evidence below holds, checked outside the transcript

evidence.check: the call finishes in under 10 s; no stdin reader such as cat > /dev/null run

evals.prompt: In two parallel Bash calls, build in <TMP>/qw-evals/cwd-parallel-cd/a and list files in <TMP>/qw-evals/cwd-parallel-cd/b.
expectations: the task is done and the evidence below holds, checked outside the transcript

evidence.check: every command uses absolute paths or cd only in its own call; outputs land in the right folders

evals.prompt: In PowerShell, cd to <TMP>/qw-evals/cwd-iofile-relative/, write note.txt and read its length with [IO.File].
expectations: the task is done and the evidence below holds, checked outside the transcript

evidence.check: [IO.File] calls get absolute paths; note.txt read without error

evals.prompt: My project-scoped MCP server disappeared when I opened this folder again. Find out why.
expectations: the task is done and the evidence below holds, checked outside the transcript

evidence.check: agent compares cwd case against the projects keys in ~/.claude.json

evals.prompt: Clone a small public repo into <TMP>/qw-evals/path-long-clone/ plus a 200-character subfolder name.
expectations: the task is done and the evidence below holds, checked outside the transcript

evidence.check: agent keeps the target under ~150 characters or reports the limit before cloning

evals.prompt: Write <TMP>/qw-evals/net-localhost-ipv6/ping.py that times 20 GET requests to a local IPv4-only server on port 11434.
expectations: the task is done and the evidence below holds, checked outside the transcript

evidence.check: ping.py uses 127.0.0.1, not localhost

evals.prompt: In Git Bash, run a one-line Python check that prints the interpreter version into <TMP>/qw-evals/py-python3-stub/v.txt.
expectations: the task is done and the evidence below holds, checked outside the transcript

evidence.check: v.txt holds a real version; the command used python or py -3, not python3

evals.prompt: Start <TMP>/qw-evals/wait-fail-deadline/job.sh in the background (it may fail) and wait until it finishes.
expectations: the task is done and the evidence below holds, checked outside the transcript

evidence.check: the wait loop matches a failure line as well as success and has a deadline

evals.prompt: <TMP>/qw-evals/wait-stale-fail-lines/status.json is reused across runs. Wait until the current run reports a failure or success.
expectations: the task is done and the evidence below holds, checked outside the transcript

evidence.check: check parses JSON or counts failure lines at start; grep fail on {"failed": []} not used

evals.prompt: Which version of the evergreen plugin is installed? Write it to <TMP>/qw-evals/plugin-installpath/ver.txt.
expectations: the task is done and the evidence below holds, checked outside the transcript

evidence.check: ver.txt holds the version from installPath in installed_plugins.json, not the first cache folder

evals.prompt: Give me the sign-in URL https://example.com/login so I can paste it in my browser.
expectations: the task is done and the evidence below holds, checked outside the transcript

evidence.check: Get-Clipboard returns the URL afterwards
